newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech shares mixed as PX50 index holds steady.
newsitem.headline: Czech shares mixed as PX50 index holds steady.

text.p: Czech shares closed mixed in heavier trading on the Prague Stock Exchange on Thursday, as the PX50 index closed unchanged at 559.8.
Utility CEZ and Komercni Banka both edged higher, but their gains were offset by losses to SPT Telecom, Skoda and Ceska Sporitelna.
Overall, 215 issues rose, 212 lost ground and 89 traded unchanged. Trading was heavier with 1.13 million shares changing hands on turnover of 1.16 billion crowns.
"We're still seeing a lot of interest in funds, but some of the other major shares are flat," said Alex Angell of Wood and Company.

Several funds have attracted heavy investor interest after declaring they would transform their closed-ended unit trusts into open-ended funds, bringing about the possibility that the shares would rise much closer to their net asset value.
Many funds, which were created during the government's massive coupon privatisation programme, trade at a deep discount.

The finance ministry is still creating guidelines for the funds to open, but at least one fund manager, Harvard, has said it plans to begin buying units from current holders in anticipation that it would receive approval to transform.
Harvard funds are trading at less than 50 percent of net asset value per share.
